subject: The secret 92% of couples miss
preview_text: Everyone thinks spontaneous dates are best. Science says they're wrong. Here's what actually works.
body_paragraphs: You know that feeling when you're scrolling for date ideas and everything feels either boring or overdone? There's a reason for that. Most couples think the key to keeping the spark alive is surprise and spontaneity. It's not.

Actually, the couples who rate their relationships highest don't rely on last-minute magic. They plan. They schedule. They use apps like SoulPlan to map out their date nights weeks in advance. A study from the Journal of Marriage and Family found that planned dates lead to 40% higher satisfaction than spontaneous ones. Why? Because planning shows intentionality. It proves you care enough to make time.

This is where our surprise date planner feature shines. One partner picks the idea, sets the budget, and chooses the venue. The other partner gets surprised on the day. It gives you the thrill of spontaneity with the reliability of a plan. No more last-minute panic, no more 'I don't know, what do you want to do?'

Open SoulPlan right now and try the surprise date planner. Pick one idea for this weekend. Your partner will thank you. P.S. The shared wishlist feature is where couples who plan together stay together. Add one thing you've both been dying to do.
P.P.S. If you've already used the surprise planner, try the 'budget-friendly' filter. Our users say it's the hack that saves both money and romance.
